meta.title: Operation of Precision Balance in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To accurately weigh crude drugs, plant powders, extract samples, and reagents to the nearest 0.001 g (1 mg) for standardization tests, extraction procedures, and phytochemical analyses.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for all weighing operations requiring precision of 1 mg or better, including moisture content determination, extractive value calculations, and preparation of standard solutions.
procedure: Ensure the precision balance is placed on a stable, vibration-free, level surface away from drafts and direct sunlight.
Check the level indicator bubble — adjust levelling feet until the bubble is centred.
Switch on the balance and allow it to warm up for at least 15–30 minutes before use (critical for accuracy).
Perform a span calibration using the internal automatic calibration function (if available) or external calibration weights as per the standard operating schedule.
Close the draught shield doors before every weighing — air currents cause reading instability.
Place a clean, dry weighing paper, boat, or container on the pan and press 'Tare' to zero the display.
Add the material to be weighed using an appropriate spatula — do not pour directly; add small portions at a time.
Wait until the display stabilizes (no flickering) before recording the weight.
Record the weight to the full precision displayed (e.g., 2.456 g — record all digits).
Remove the sample and the weighing vessel; close the draught shield and press 'Tare' to verify zero return.
For corrosive or hygroscopic materials, weigh quickly and use sealed containers or weighing by difference.
Clean the pan after each use with a soft brush or lint-free cloth — never use water directly on the pan.
Record all weighing operations in the laboratory register: date, balance ID, material, and weight.
Switch off the balance after use; clean the draught shield glass with a dry cloth.
precautions: Never exceed the maximum capacity of the balance — overloading damages the load cell permanently.
Always close the draught shield before weighing — even slight air movement causes significant error at milligram precision.
Do not place hot objects on the pan — thermal gradients cause erroneous readings.
Calibrate the balance at the beginning of each day or after moving the instrument.
Handle calibration weights with forceps only — finger contact deposits oils that alter weight.
Keep chemicals away from the internal mechanism — spilled chemicals corrode the weighing cell.
Do not press on the pan — use a spatula to add material gently.
Record the balance ID number in all weighing logs for traceability.
